aboutLead: I used to build screens. Now I write the questions.
aboutBody: I worked as a frontend developer for three and a half years at a B2B2C startup in Korea, building products close to the customer.
I once built a Chrome extension that pulled in Instagram reviews the backend couldn't reach. It was used over 100 times a week, and several customers thanked me. It was my proudest moment on the job.

Around then, I could see AI changing how software gets built. I brought Cursor into the company first and encouraged everyone to try AI. After trying vibe coding myself, I was convinced AI would soon handle much of frontend work.

So I went back to what I had always loved: math, where every correct method lands on the same answer; building and improving a defined design; and the joy of customers responding. BA is where those three meet, and I judged it would take AI a long time to fully replace business insight.

Now I'm studying data analytics in Vancouver. I set the question first, then check whether an insight is statistically significant. A claim backed by evidence persuades. When an answer comes back without significance, I call it what it is, no finding, and look for another route.
AI agents are my team. I decide what to hand off and what to look at myself.
